source.title: Successful retries are not retained when saving successful executions is disabled

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

When saving successful production executions is disabled, a retry that finishes successfully is also discarded. The original failed execution can remain without a `retrySuccessId`, even though it has been retried successfully.

This happens both when retrying manually through the UI and when using the public API.

As a result, execution history does not reliably indicate which failures have been resolved. Retry automation that checks `retrySuccessId` can select the same failed execution again and repeat operations that have already succeeded.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a **Webhook → Code** sequence.
2. Enable saving failed production executions and disable saving successful production executions.
3. Configure the Code node to fail:
   ```javascript
   throw new Error('Retry retention test');
   ```
4. Publish the workflow and call its production webhook to create a failed execution.
5. Change the Code node to:
   ```javascript
   return $input.all();
   ```
6. Save the workflow.
7. Open the failed execution in the UI and retry it using the currently saved workflow.
8. Observe that the retry succeeds, but its result is not retained and the original execution may still have no `retrySuccessId`.

The same behavior can be reproduced through the API:

```http
POST /api/v1/executions/<failed-execution-id>/retry
Content-Type: application/json
X-N8N-API-KEY: <api-key>

{"loadWorkflow": true}
```

### Expected behavior

Successful retry executions should remain available even when saving ordinary successful executions is disabled.

The original failed execution should reference the retained successful retry through `retrySuccessId`, allowing users and automation to distinguish resolved failures from executions that still need attention.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
This is an accurate catch. The issue is that the runner's execution persistence policy evaluates the child retry independently: because `EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_SUCCESS=none`, the child record is dropped before or without committing the foreign key update (`execution_entity.retrySuccessId`) back onto the parent failed execution.

Until core decouples retry-lineage tracking from raw success retention, two practical workarounds:
1. Enable `EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_SUCCESS=all` paired with aggressive pruning (`EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE=24` or lower) so metadata is written and settled before being pruned.
2. If retrying via API, check the synchronous response of `POST /api/v1/executions/{id}/retry` directly for `status: "success"` and track settled parent IDs in an external set/cache rather than polling `retrySuccessId` from n8n's DB.

comments.author: epistemedeus
comments.text:
I checked the public retry API on n8n 2.46.6 (regular mode, SQLite), with a separate synthetic HTTP destination. This confirms the API-response workaround when the response arrives, and shows where it stops helping.

- With successful-run storage off, the retry response returned `status: success`, a new execution ID, and `retryOf` pointing to the failed execution. A later GET of the child returned 404, and the failed execution had no `retrySuccessId`.
- In a second test I disconnected the caller before the destination finished. It still completed once. With storage off, the public history read showed no success link or new execution. With storage on, the original linked to a readable successful child. Neither test resent the retry.

So if the retry response is lost, an empty history read is not enough to decide to retry again. Check the destination by its original reference if it supports one. This is a released-version baseline, not a test of #43925.

[Runnable test with both retention settings](https://gist.github.com/epistemedeus/3bfb06a2c263d2fc741a5acc3856379c/acad00a6ceb69c321f269284e16863ad21a77add).
